reasoning_traces.think:
The analysis begins by defining the league home field advantage (LHFA) as the mean score differential between home and away games across all teams and seasons from 2006–2020, yielding a value of 2.85 points. This is modeled using a fixed-effect binary variable for 'home' in a regression framework. Team-specific HFA (iHFA) is derived through a random slope within teams, capturing deviations from the league average. The true HFA for any team is computed as the sum of LHFA and iHFA. Adjustments for team strength, quarterback performance, and head coach competence are made using fixed effects to isolate pure HFA. Failure modes include non-statistically significant iHFA values, which lead to reverting to the league average. The methodological novelty lies in treating each team’s performance in each game separately, enabling ceteris paribus comparisons. This allows for robust estimation of HFA even under varying conditions such as coaching changes or quarterback transitions.
